chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: Harper, Sure as You're Born and title songs
summary: Mandel says Harper's theme became a song only because every film turned its theme into one, a practice he dates to High Noon and Laura.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now, so, after, The Russians are Coming, came, Harper, with Paul Newman, from which came, “Sure as You’re Born.”
Um-hm, which was never meant to be a song but somehow became because that was the era where they turned everything into a song, they just put a lyric to it.
Do you think that the success that Mancini had with some of the songs that came from his movies had something to do with that? Things like, “Moon River, “ and, “Charade,” and what have you?

No, that started a long time ago in 1952 with the title song when Dimitri Tiomkin wrote, “High Noon.” The title song was really with us all through the 50s and it wasn’t necessarily a good thing but it was a good thing for song writers.
I guess even earlier with, “Laura,” for example.
That was a freak ‘cause it started life as an instrumental theme, it wasn’t even sung in the movie.
And Johnny Mercer wrote a lyric to it later on.
